argument_summary: The admissible record supports a conditional certification position, not a clean unqualified one. Evidence shows aggregate launch readiness is met (BMCARD-020-A), the small-business support slice underperforms its thresholds (BMCARD-020-B), policy requires disclosure of a material weakness unless an approved mitigation removes exposure (BMCARD-020-C), small-sample uncertainty lowers confidence but does not eliminate the weakness (BMCARD-020-D), and the proposed monitoring mitigation is unapproved (BMCARD-020-E). On that basis, the defensible packet is: certify_model only with explicit model-card disclosure of the slice weakness and without treating draft monitoring as a substitute.
claims_about_policy: Policy permits certification when material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes exposure. The same policy also says aggregate pass rates do not erase subgroup weaknesses, and small-sample uncertainty does not convert an unresolved material weakness into clean certification. Therefore the audited claim should be read as a caveated certification basis conditioned on disclosure, not as evidence of already completed clean compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost override is needed to justify this position. The risk-weighted reading of the admissible evidence already supports avoiding escalation to a deployment block, provided the certification outcome is narrowed to explicit disclosure-conditioned compliance.
concessions: The present evidentiary record does not prove that the final model card already contains the required disclosure.
The record does not support any implication that certification is presently clean or unconditional.
The draft post-launch monitoring proposal cannot currently reduce or remove exposure because it is unapproved.
